answer: The inlet multiplier is published, charged in grove, and oasis lists each payment. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 14 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. A farm of 3051 identities would post 729 proofs and burn roughly 11 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
